subtitle: Your travel footprint
promotionalText: Watch every country you've been to fill in on a living globe. Find them in your photos, log your flights and see how much of the world you've seen.
description:
Terris shades the countries you've been to on a globe and gives you one honest number: how much of the world you've seen.

YOUR WORLD, SHADED
Mark a country Visited, Lived or Want to go and it fills in on the globe. Spin it, tap a country, and see your count out of all 197 countries, with a breakdown by continent.

FOUND IN YOUR PHOTOS
Terris can read where your photos were taken and suggest the countries for you. It all happens on your iPhone: your photos are never uploaded, and nothing is added until you say so.

EVERY COUNTRY HAS A PAGE
Your newest photo from there, the cities you went to, your first and last visit, your notes, and three facts you might not know.

EVERY FLIGHT, EVERY MILE
Log your flights and see your routes drawn on the map, the distance you've flown and how far around the Earth that is.

DAY AND NIGHT
A bright, airy look by day and a glowing night map in dark mode. Three ways to see your world: Globe, Journal or Atlas. On iPhone and iPad.

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
No account, no tracking, no ads. Your map syncs only through your own iCloud.

testflight.description: Terris shades the countries you've been to on a globe and counts how much of the world you've seen. Mark countries by hand or let Terris find them in your photos (on your iPhone, never uploaded), keep a page for each country, and log your flights. Your map syncs through your own iCloud; there's no account and no tracking.
testflight.whatToTest:
The new look: bright Immersive Glass by day and the glowing Night Atlas in dark mode (switch your iPhone's appearance to see both).

- Map: the big count, the globe (spin it, tap a country), the glass buttons on the right and the sheet you can pull up.
- A country's page: your newest photo (or the outline) at the top, the status picker, cities, photos, notes and Did you know.
- Flights: the route map, the distance and the bar towards one lap of the Earth.

Tell us anything that looks off, in light or dark.
